targets.speaker: ALEX
targets.target: When does a viral dev tool stop being a toy and start becoming leverage?

targets.speaker: JAMIE
targets.target: The simple version is this: when a small tool or clone changes what builders can ship, copy, automate, or replace.

targets.speaker: JAMIE
targets.target: The scary part is not the average result. It is the person, patient, team, or company living inside the exception.

targets.speaker: RUFUS
targets.target: Lovely. We have automated the decision and preserved the blame. Very efficient, in the bleakest possible sense.

targets.speaker: JAMIE
targets.target: Think of it like one clever repo turning into a forklift for every developer who was previously carrying boxes by hand.

targets.speaker: ALEX
targets.target: Do not ask only what launched. Ask what new permission, risk, cost, or accountability chain just appeared.

targets.speaker: RUFUS
targets.target: The question for tomorrow is not whether developer leverage sounds clever. It is who gets caught when it becomes real.
